- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥1.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-1.0), model underestimates; adjust downward by 3–7% to avoid missing downside momentum.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes; apply a 1–2 day lag correction for price reversals after sharp increases.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show rising prices, reduce forecast slope; if falling, increase slope to reflect momentum reversal.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model often overestimates late-period prices (last 7–10 days); apply downward bias of 2–5% for final 10 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
